title: Vocabulary & Language
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah memiliki pengetahuan dasar untuk memberikan informasi terkait rutinitas dan kebiasaan.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 32-34
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will learn new words about daily routines and habits.
Learners will be able to understand, identify, and say key vocabulary about daily routines and habits.
Learners will be able to ask and answer questions about when they do habits and routines.

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
The teacher introduces himself/herself in front of the class.
Get to know the students by using the letter game.
The teacher writes down his/her name on the board (e.g. Susan)
Ask the student if their name starts with the shown letter (e.g. starts with S) and then they must stand up and introduce themselves. Continue with other letters.
Other alternatives to get to know the students: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at the pictures and questions on page 32.
Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to talk about what they can see in the pictures. Elicit some ideas from the group and write down any key words on the board.
Tell students they have 5-6 minutes to discuss the questions. Encourage them to use English, but if they don’t have enough vocabulary, it’s acceptable to use some words in their first language.
The teacher can also write their answers on the board or show them on the screen.
After 5-6 minutes, stop the task and elicit some ideas from students.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 33 and ask the class, “What can you see on the page?”
Tell students that they will do a listening task. They need to listen and write the number in each box according to the order they hear in the audio.
Before playing the audio, read all of the words together and teachers could ask simple questions to check understanding.
Play audio 4.1. If needed, the teacher can pause the audio after track 1 to check that the students understand how to do the task. Then, continue with the audio.
Ask students to check their answers with a partner.
Check the answers together. Write the correct answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Continue until all answers are checked. Ask students to read the sentences from the audio script aloud, in pairs.
This activity is for pronunciation practice.
Tell students to listen and repeat the words they hear.
Play audio 4.2 and encourage students to repeat the words loudly, and encourage them to try to copy the intonation they hear in the audio.
For variation, vocabulary drilling can be done in groups, pairs, loudly, quietly, etc.
Ask students to look in their books at the Vocabulary C task and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Do the first number together as a class to make sure students understand what to do.
Put students in pairs and ask them to complete the task in around 5 minutes.
Then, check the answers. Write the answers on the board or show them on the screen using the PPT for this book.
Ask students to read the completed sentences aloud to each other, in pairs.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
The teacher mimes one of the activities in activity A, and students must try to guess the activity.
The first student who guesses correctly comes and stands in front of the class.
They mime another activity shown in activity A on this page and other students must try to guess the activity.
The first student who guesses correctly comes and stands in front of the class.
Repeat until all activities have been mimed and guessed correctly.
Ask students to open their Student Book to page 34.
First, the teacher reads the Q&A models in the speech bubbles at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the Q&A models aloud as a class.
Then, the teacher asks students to read the Q&A models together in pairs (Ask and answer the questions with a partner).

This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs. Encourage students to change the key vocabulary in the questions and answers, by using the vocabulary learned on the previous page
Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes). This can be used to help answer students' questions.
Ask students to look at the practice task B.
Tell students to circle two mistakes in every sentence. Remind students to use the Q&A models at the top of the page and the Language Box at the bottom of the page to help guide them.
Put students in pairs and give them around 4-5 minutes to complete the task.
Check the answers. Write the answers on the board.
Read the completed sentences aloud together as a class.
To make the checking answer stage more fun, teachers could let the students choose their own classmates to answer the next question by passing a marker or tossing a paper ball.
Ask students to write four sentences about when they do different routines. They should do this individually.
Write the following sentence pattern on the board:
Tell students to use this sentence pattern to write their four sentences.
Next, put students in pairs and tell them to read their sentences aloud to each other.
Elicit some responses from individual students to share with the whole class.
Choose 1-2 students to share their habits/routines.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: pengamatan pelafalan saat drill kosakata (listen and repeat).
Pemeriksaan jawaban latihan kosakata dan language practice di Student Book.
Unjuk kerja lisan: peserta didik memakai kosakata & struktur baru dalam kalimat sendiri.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
